items.title: Japan's foreign reserves drop by a record $80 billion in August following yen intervention
items.body: Finance ministry data showed that Japan's official foreign reserves stand at $1.207 trillion, down from July's figure of $1.287 trillion.

items.title: From ‘mystery vacations’ to hostels, budget travelers get thrifty as prices rise
items.body: Despite rising prices and the travel industry focusing on the luxury segment, budget-minded vacationers are still finding ways to get away.

items.title: Trump turns up the heat on Warsh as Fed rate hike looms
items.body: Ten days ahead of the next Federal Reserve meeting, the Trump administration looks to be in a full-court press to halt a rate hike in its tracks.

items.title: Women accounted for almost all of job gains in August. Here's why
items.body: Women accounted for virtually all of August's payroll gains, the latest sign of their growing power in the labor market.

items.title: U.S. payrolls rose 162,000 in August, much more than expected; unemployment rate at 4.1%
items.body: Nonfarm payrolls were expected to increase by 53,000 in August while the unemployment rate held at 4.1%, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

items.title: The big business of personal protection: How private security became a $50 billion industry
items.body: Private security spending and guard employment have climbed as companies and communities respond to high-profile attacks, even as violent crime falls.

items.title: The big August jobs report is due out Friday. Here's what to expect for what has been a jobless summer
items.body: August nonfarm payrolls are expected to rise by 53,000 as a subdued labor market keeps Fed attention focused on inflation.

items.title: Fed Governor Waller indicates he will support holding rates steady at September meeting
items.body: In remarks that seem to contrast with statements last week from Chairman Kevin Warsh, Waller expressed confidence in the current inflation trends.
